title.zh: 卷328 列傳一百十五 常青 蓝元枚 蔡攀龙 梁朝桂 普吉保 丁朝雄 鄂辉 舒亮
title.en: Volume 328 Biographies 115: Chang Qing, Lan Yuanmei, Cai Panlong, Liang Chaogui, Pu Ji Bao, Ding Chaoxiong, E Hui, Shu Liang
title.raw: 卷328 列傳一百十五 常青 蓝元枚 蔡攀龙 梁朝桂 普吉保 丁朝雄 鄂辉 舒亮

sentences.zh: 列傳一百十五

translations.literal: Biographies 115
translations.idiomatic: Biography 115

sentences.zh: 常青，佟佳氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Chang Qing, of the Tunggiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Qing, of the Tunggiya clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 父安圖，官至江西巡撫。

translations.literal: His father Antu reached the office of Governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Antu had served as governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 常青自寧郡王府長史累遷察哈爾都統，杭州、福州將軍。

translations.literal: Chang Qing rose in succession from Chief steward of the Ning Commandery Prince's establishment to Commander-in-chief of Chahar, and to General at Hangzhou and Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Qing advanced step by step from chief steward in the Ning commandery prince's household to commander-in-chief of Chahar and then to general at Hangzhou and Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十一年，署閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Qianlong, he acted as Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 51 (1786), he was appointed acting governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 諸羅縣民楊光勳與其弟爭家業，糾眾立會，縣吏捕治不服，常青令按察使李永祺往按。

translations.literal: Yang Guangxun, a commoner of Zhuluo County, disputed the family estate with his younger brother, gathered a crowd to form a secret society, and when county officials arrested and punished them they would not submit; Chang Qing ordered Surveillance Commissioner Li Yongqi to go investigate.
translations.idiomatic: A Zhuluo county man named Yang Guangxun feuded with his brother over family property, rallied supporters into a sworn association, and resisted arrest when county officials moved against them; Chang Qing dispatched surveillance commissioner Li Yongqi to investigate.

sentences.zh: 上以台灣在海外，不可輕縱，諭勿使蔓延疏脫。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Taiwan was beyond the sea, said it could not be lightly indulged, and instructed that it must not be allowed to spread or slip through lax handling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor considered Taiwan distant and unstable territory that could not be treated lightly, and ordered that the affair must not be allowed to spread or escape control through negligence.

sentences.zh: 尋實授閩浙總督。

translations.literal: Soon he was formally appointed Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon confirmed in the post of governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，林爽文亂起，陷彰化，知縣俞峻死之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the rebellion of Lin Shuangwen arose; Zhanghua fell, and Magistrate Yu Jun died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Lin Shuangwen uprising broke out; Zhanghua was taken and magistrate Yu Jun was killed.

sentences.zh: 常青檄水師提督黃仕簡自鹿耳門進，副將丁朝雄從海壇鎮總兵郝壯猷自淡水進，都司馬元勳屯鹿仔港，分道部署；

translations.literal: Chang Qing ordered Naval Commander-in-chief Huang Shijian to advance from Luerhmen, Vice-general Ding Chaoxiong to accompany Haizhen garrison commander-in-chief Hao Zhuangyou advancing from Tamsui, and Department Commander Ma Yuanxun to encamp at Lugang, deploying forces along separate routes;
translations.idiomatic: Chang Qing directed naval commander-in-chief Huang Shijian to enter from Luerhmen, vice-general Ding Chaoxiong to move with Haizhen garrison commander Hao Zhuangyou from Tamsui, and department commander Ma Yuanxun to hold Lugang, dividing his forces along several axes.

sentences.zh: 復如泉州會陸路提督任承恩調度，令金門鎮總兵羅英笈詣廈門彈壓。

translations.literal: He then went to Quanzhou to confer with Land Forces Commander-in-chief Ren Chengen on deployment, and ordered Kinmen garrison commander-in-chief Luo Yingji to proceed to Xiamen to suppress unrest.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Quanzhou to coordinate with land-forces commander Ren Chengen and ordered Kinmen garrison commander Luo Yingji to Xiamen to keep order.

sentences.zh: 尋復令承恩自鹿耳門繼進。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again ordered Chengen to follow up by advancing from Luerhmen.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he ordered Chengen to press forward again from Luerhmen.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，奏賊陷諸羅。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year, he memorialized that the rebels had taken Zhuluo.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 52 (1787) he reported that the rebels had captured Zhuluo.

sentences.zh: 台灣鎮總兵柴大紀堵剿，賊勢稍沮。

translations.literal: Taiwan garrison commander-in-chief Chai Daji blocked and suppressed them, and the rebel momentum slackened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan garrison commander Chai Daji held them in check, and rebel strength began to falter.

sentences.zh: 爽文漳州人，其徒率漳籍。

translations.literal: Shuangwen was a native of Zhangzhou, and his followers were mostly men of Zhangzhou registration.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen was from Zhangzhou, and most of his followers were Zhangzhou men.

sentences.zh: 移會兩廣督臣防範，上責其張皇。

translations.literal: He forwarded a joint notice to the governors of Guangdong and Guangxi to take precautions, and the emperor rebuked him for alarmism.
translations.idiomatic: He notified the governors of the two Guang provinces to guard against spillover, and the emperor criticized him for overstating the danger.

sentences.zh: 授李侍堯閩浙總督，而移常青湖廣。

translations.literal: Li Shiyao was appointed Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang, while Chang Qing was transferred to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiyao was made governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang, and Chang Qing was reassigned to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 既又命常青渡台視師，四月，至台灣。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was again ordered to cross to Taiwan to oversee the army; in the fourth month he reached Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered back to cross to Taiwan and take command of the campaign; in the fourth month he arrived on the island.

sentences.zh: 劾仕簡、承恩遷延觀望，擁兵自衛；

translations.literal: He impeached Shijian and Chengen for delay and watching from the sidelines while holding troops for their own protection;
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Shijian and Chengen for dragging their feet, holding back while hoarding troops for self-protection;

sentences.zh: 壯猷守鳳山，賊至，棄城走。

translations.literal: Zhuangyou was defending Fengshan; when the rebels arrived, he abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangyou was holding Fengshan; when rebels came he abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 諭逮承恩，罷仕簡候命，而誅壯猷，遂授常青為將軍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chengen arrested, Shijian dismissed pending orders, and Zhuangyou executed; then Chang Qing was appointed General.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Chengen arrested, relieved Shijian pending further orders, and executed Zhuangyou; Chang Qing was then appointed general.

sentences.zh: 賊攻府城，常青督諸軍禦戰，有所俘馘；

translations.literal: The rebels attacked the prefectural city; Chang Qing directed the armies in defense and took some captives and heads;
translations.idiomatic: When rebels assaulted the prefectural seat, Chang Qing led the troops in defense and won some captives and heads;

sentences.zh: 賊攻桶盤棧，令游擊蔡攀龍等分駐力禦。

translations.literal: When the rebels attacked Tongpanzhan, he ordered Guerrilla Commander Cai Panlong and others to station forces separately and resist with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels attacked Tongpanzhan, he posted guerrilla commander Cai Panlong and others at separate points to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 奏入，上以常青年逾七十，能如此勇往督戰，手詔嘉獎，授其子刑部筆帖式喜明三等侍衛，馳驛往省，並賜御用搬指。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor, because Chang Qing was over seventy yet could press forward so boldly in directing battle, personally wrote an edict of praise, appointed his son Ximing, a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, as a third-rank bodyguard, sent him post-haste to visit his father, and also bestowed an imperial thumb ring.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached court, the emperor praised Chang Qing in a personal edict for pressing the fight at over seventy, made his son Ximing—a Ministry of Punishments clerk—a third-rank bodyguard, sent him post-haste to visit his father, and granted an imperial thumb ring.

sentences.zh: 旋奏爽文還大里杙舊巢，其徒莊大田等萬餘人分擾南路，擬先南剿大田，乃北取爽文。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized that Shuangwen had returned to his old lair at Daliyi, while his followers Zhuang Datian and others, more than ten thousand men, were raiding the southern route in separate bands; he proposed first to suppress Datian in the south, then to strike north and take Shuangwen.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported that Shuangwen had withdrawn to his old base at Daliyi while followers such as Zhuang Datian, numbering more than ten thousand, were harrying the south; he planned to crush Datian in the south first, then move north against Shuangwen.

sentences.zh: 上韙之，下部優敘。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it and ordered the ministries to record meritorious service favorably.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan and ordered a favorable record of merit in the ministries.

sentences.zh: 旋奏勦賊南潭，殲賊六百餘；

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized on suppressing rebels at Nantan, annihilating more than six hundred rebels;
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported a campaign at Nantan in which more than six hundred rebels were killed;

sentences.zh: 爽文之徒莊錫舍出降，擒偽軍師番婦金孃，請檻車送京師，上命授錫舍守備。

translations.literal: Shuangwen's follower Zhuang Xishe came over in surrender; the false strategist, the aboriginal woman Jin Niang, was captured; he requested sending her to the capital in a caged cart; the emperor ordered Xishe appointed garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen's follower Zhuang Xishe defected, and the rebels' female aboriginal strategist Jin Niang was taken; he asked to send her to the capital in a prison cart, and the emperor made Xishe a garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 又奏進剿鳳山，出城未十里，賊三面並進，官兵奮勇擊退；

translations.literal: He again memorialized on advancing to suppress Fengshan; not ten li outside the city, rebels pressed in from three sides, and government troops fought them off with spirit;
translations.idiomatic: He reported another advance on Fengshan; less than ten li from the city rebels closed in from three directions, and government troops drove them back;

sentences.zh: 賊勢蔓延，請厚集兵力，遣大臣督戰。

translations.literal: As rebel strength spread, he requested concentrating more troops and dispatching a high minister to direct the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: With rebel strength spreading, he asked for heavier reinforcements and a senior minister to take command.

sentences.zh: 上命陝甘總督福康安往視師。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Fuk'anggan to go oversee the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general Fuk'anggan to take command of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 旋奏：「賊犯府城，為丁朝雄擊退。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized: "The rebels attacked the prefectural city and were beaten back by Ding Chaoxiong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported: "Rebels assaulted the prefectural seat and were repulsed by Ding Chaoxiong.

sentences.zh: 官軍攻莊大田於南潭，殺賊二百餘。

translations.literal: Government troops attacked Zhuang Datian at Nantan and killed more than two hundred rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces attacked Zhuang Datian at Nantan and killed more than two hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 大營距府城未遠，勢相犄角，無後顧之虞。」

translations.literal: The main camp was not far from the prefectural city, the positions mutually supporting like horn and corner, with no worry for the rear."
translations.idiomatic: The main camp lay close enough to the prefectural seat to support it in mutual defense, with no concern for the rear."

sentences.zh: 得旨嘉獎，賜雙眼孔雀翎。

translations.literal: He received an edict of praise and was granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised him in an edict and awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 旋迭奏鹽水港、笨港均為賊據，糧道既斷，諸羅勢甚危；

translations.literal: Soon he repeatedly memorialized that Yanshui Harbor and Bengang were both held by rebels, the grain route was cut, and Zhuluo was in grave peril;
translations.idiomatic: He soon sent repeated reports that Yanshui Harbor and Bengang had fallen to rebels, supply lines were cut, and Zhuluo was in dire straits;

sentences.zh: 令總兵魏大斌赴援，戰賊失利，又令游擊田藍玉援大斌。

translations.literal: He ordered Commander-in-chief Wei Dabin to go to the relief; in fighting the rebels he was defeated, and he then ordered Guerrilla Commander Tian Lanyu to reinforce Dabin.
translations.idiomatic: He sent commander Wei Dabin to relieve the city, but Dabin was beaten in action; he then ordered guerrilla commander Tian Lanyu to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 上以兵分力薄，飭常青調度失當。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the forces were divided and too thin, rebuked Chang Qing for faulty deployment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Chang Qing for poor coordination, saying his forces were spread too thin.

sentences.zh: 又諭：「常青駐軍桶盤棧，距南潭不過五里，不將賊目莊大田先行剿除，乃結營自守。

translations.literal: He further instructed: "Chang Qing encamped at Tongpanzhan, no more than five li from Nantan, yet did not first wipe out the rebel leader Zhuang Datian, but instead entrenched himself in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: The court also said: "Chang Qing held Tongpanzhan only five li from Nantan yet failed to destroy the rebel chief Zhuang Datian first, instead digging in on the defensive.

sentences.zh: 肘腋之間，任其逼處。」

translations.literal: At his very armpit he allowed the enemy to press close."
translations.idiomatic: He let the enemy press in at his very side."

sentences.zh: 八月，命福康安為將軍，督諸將海蘭察、普爾普等大出師討爽文。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Fuk'anggan was appointed General and directed the generals Hailancha, Pulupu, and others in a major expedition against Shuangwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Fuk'anggan was made general and led Hailancha, Pulupu, and other commanders in a full-scale campaign against Shuangwen.

sentences.zh: 諭常青，謂：「非責其師無功，特以年已七十，軍旅非所素習。

translations.literal: Chang Qing was instructed: "This is not to blame you for achieving nothing as commander, but simply that you are already seventy, and military affairs are not what you have long practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Qing was told: "This is not to reproach you for failure in command, but at seventy you are not seasoned in field warfare.

sentences.zh: 福康安未至，仍當相機進​​剿。」

translations.literal: Before Fuk'anggan arrives, you should still advance to suppress as opportunity permits."
translations.idiomatic: Until Fuk'anggan arrives, you should still press the attack whenever conditions allow."

sentences.zh: 旋奏：「賊自南潭來攻，侍衛烏什哈達等擊敗之。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized: "Rebels attacked from Nantan and were defeated by Bodyguard Ushihada and others.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported: "Rebels came from Nantan and were beaten back by bodyguard Ushihada and others.

sentences.zh: 因雨後路滑，收兵；

translations.literal: Because the roads were slippery after rain, the troops were withdrawn;
translations.idiomatic: After rain made the roads treacherous, the troops were pulled back;

sentences.zh: 又進攻南潭，焚草藔數百間，以天晚，山徑偪仄，不便深入。」

translations.literal: they again advanced on Nantan and burned several hundred thatched huts; as night fell, the mountain paths were narrow and cramped, making deep pursuit inconvenient."
translations.idiomatic: they advanced again on Nantan and burned several hundred rebel huts; at dusk the mountain trails were too narrow for a deep pursuit."

sentences.zh: 藔謂賊所居草屋也。

translations.literal: Liao means the grass huts where the rebels lived.
translations.idiomatic: Liao here means the grass huts in which the rebels dwelt.

sentences.zh: 上以其屢稱遇雨路仄收兵，傳旨嚴飭。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he repeatedly cited rain, bad roads, and narrow paths as reasons for withdrawing troops, sent an edict sternly rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, weary of repeated excuses about rain, mud, and narrow trails, sent a stern rebuke.

sentences.zh: 上又聞賊诇知軍中暑濕多病，常青機事不密，又不督兵深入，屢詰責。

translations.literal: The emperor also heard that the rebels had learned by espionage that the army suffered much from heat, damp, and disease; that Chang Qing was not discreet in his plans; and that he again failed to drive the troops deep—he was repeatedly questioned and rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: The court also learned that rebels had spied out the army's heat-sickness and that Chang Qing's plans leaked and he would not drive troops forward; he was rebuked again and again.

sentences.zh: 旋奏總兵梁朝桂勦賊多斬獲，提督柴大紀報諸羅圍急，令副將蔡攀龍赴援。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized that Commander-in-chief Liang Chaogui had suppressed rebels with many kills and captures; Commander-in-chief Chai Daji reported that the siege of Zhuluo was urgent; he ordered Vice-general Cai Panlong to go to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: He reported commander Liang Chaogui's heavy kills in action and commander Chai Daji's urgent plea from the Zhuluo siege, and sent vice-general Cai Panlong to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 上諭令親援大紀，待福康安至，合軍進攻。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him to go in person to relieve Daji, and when Fuk'anggan arrived to join forces and attack.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to relieve Daji in person and, once Fuk'anggan arrived, to combine forces for a general assault.

sentences.zh: 旋奏同江寧將軍永慶等在竹篙厝等處殲賊甚眾；

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized that together with Jiangning General Yongqing and others he had annihilated very many rebels at Zhugaocuo and other places;
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported that with Jiangning general Yongqing and others he had destroyed large rebel forces at Zhugaocuo and elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 山豬毛社義民尤趫捷，獲砲一，生擒賊目張招。

translations.literal: the loyal militia of the Shanzhumao community were especially swift and agile; one cannon was captured and the rebel leader Zhang Zhao was taken alive.
translations.idiomatic: loyal militia from the Shanzhumao community fought with exceptional speed; one cannon was taken and rebel leader Zhang Zhao captured alive.

sentences.zh: 又奏總兵普吉保克月眉莊，距諸羅五里，令與大紀並力固守；

translations.literal: He again memorialized that Commander-in-chief Pu Jibao had taken Yuemeizhuang, five li from Zhuluo, and he ordered him to hold fast together with Daji;
translations.idiomatic: He reported that commander Pu Jibao had taken Yuemeizhuang, five li from Zhuluo, and ordered him to hold the line with Daji;

sentences.zh: 又令諸生劉宗榮等給番社土目札諭防賊竄匿。

translations.literal: he also ordered the students Liu Zongrong and others to issue written notices to aboriginal community headmen to guard against rebels slipping into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: and had students Liu Zongrong and others deliver written orders to aboriginal headmen to block rebel escape routes.

sentences.zh: 屢得旨嘉許。

translations.literal: He repeatedly received edicts of approval.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised these reports repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 福康安渡台灣。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan crossed to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan crossed to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 上授常青福州將軍，留辦善後，令從將軍職戴單眼孔雀翎。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Chang Qing General at Fuzhou, to remain and handle aftermath, ordering him to retain the general's rank while wearing the single-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Chang Qing general at Fuzhou to stay behind for pacification, allowing him to keep general's rank with the single-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 福康安劾大紀貪劣狀，上責常青徇隱，奪職，交福康安嚴鞫。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan impeached Daji for corruption and misconduct; the emperor blamed Chang Qing for shielding him, stripped his office, and handed him over to Fuk'anggan for strict interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuk'anggan impeached Daji for corruption, the emperor blamed Chang Qing for covering for him, stripped his post, and turned him over to Fuk'anggan for trial.

sentences.zh: 福康安旋以常青自承徇隱，請交部治罪，上特宥之。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan soon reported that Chang Qing had himself confessed to shielding wrongdoing and asked that he be handed to the ministries for punishment; the emperor specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan reported Chang Qing's confession of covering for Daji and asked the ministries to punish him, but the emperor pardoned him outright.

sentences.zh: 召詣京師，署鑲紅旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital and acted as Commander-in-chief of the Mongol Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital and served as acting commander of the Mongol Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，授禮部尚書、鑲藍旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he was appointed Minister of Rites and Commander-in-chief of the Han Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 54 (1789) he was made minister of rites and commander of the Han Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，卒，諡恭簡。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he died; his posthumous title was Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianlong 58 (1793) and was given the posthumous name Gongjian.

sentences.zh: 子喜明，官至徐州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: His son Ximing rose to the post of Commander-in-chief of the Xuzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ximing rose to commander of the Xuzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 常青初視師，福州將軍恆瑞，水陸二提督任承恩、黃仕簡皆在行，戰無功。

translations.literal: When Chang Qing first took command, Fuzhou General Hengrui and the two commanders-in-chief of land and naval forces, Ren Chengen and Huang Shijian, were all in the field, yet achieved nothing in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Qing first took the field, Fuzhou general Hengrui and land and naval commanders Ren Chengen and Huang Shijian were all present yet won no victories.

sentences.zh: 承恩、仕簡以誤軍機坐斬，台灣平，赦出獄。

translations.literal: Chengen and Shijian were sentenced to decapitation for military failure; when Taiwan was pacified they were pardoned and released from prison.
translations.idiomatic: Chengen and Shijian had been condemned to death for military failure; after Taiwan was pacified they were pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 仕簡至狼山鎮總兵，承恩亦至副將，恆瑞自有傳。

translations.literal: Shijian rose to Commander-in-chief of the Langshan garrison, and Chengen also reached Vice-general; Hengrui has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shijian eventually became Langshan garrison commander and Chengen a vice-general; Hengrui has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 藍元枚，字簡侯，福建漳浦人，提督廷珍孫。

translations.literal: Lan Yuanmei, style name Jianhou, was a native of Zhangpu in Fujian, and grandson of Commander-in-chief Tingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Yuanmei (style Jianhou), a native of Zhangpu in Fujian, was grandson of commander Tingzhen.

sentences.zh: 父日寵，官福建銅山營水師參將。

translations.literal: His father Richong held the post of Naval Deputy Commander of the Tongshan camp in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Richong had been naval deputy commander of the Fujian Tongshan camp.

sentences.zh: 元枚襲三等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: Yuanmei inherited the hereditary office of third-rank Chariot Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmei inherited the hereditary rank of third-class chariot commandant.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年，命發廣東，以外海水師參將用，補海門營參將。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong he was ordered sent to Guangdong and employed as Deputy Commander of the outer-sea naval forces, filling the post of Deputy Commander of the Haimen camp.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 31 (1766) he was sent to Guangdong as an outer-sea naval deputy commander and appointed to the Haimen camp.

sentences.zh: 累遷總兵，歷台灣、金門、蘇松三鎮。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Commander-in-chief, serving in the three garrisons of Taiwan, Kinmen, and Susong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to garrison commander and served at Taiwan, Kinmen, and Susong.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，授江南提督。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he was appointed Commander-in-chief of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 49 (1784) he was made commander of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 五十二年正月，台灣民林爽文為亂，命元枚馳驛往泉州，署福建陸路提督，駐蚶江策應。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifty-second year the Taiwan commoner Lin Shuangwen rose in rebellion; Yuanmei was ordered post-haste to Quanzhou, acted as Land Forces Commander-in-chief of Fujian, and encamped at Hanjiang to coordinate support.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianlong 52 (1787) Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan; Yuanmei was rushed to Quanzhou as acting Fujian land-forces commander, encamping at Hanjiang to support the campaign.

sentences.zh: 至福州，奏言：「師渡台灣，亂民潰散，慮入內山與生番勾結。」

translations.literal: Reaching Fuzhou, he memorialized: "When the army crosses to Taiwan the rebels will scatter, but I fear they may flee into the inner mountains and join with the raw aborigines."
translations.idiomatic: At Fuzhou he reported: "Once troops cross to Taiwan the rebels will scatter, but they may flee into the interior hills and ally with aboriginal tribes."

sentences.zh: 上諭令速捕治，俾盡根株。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed that they be swiftly arrested and punished so that the roots might be wholly extirpated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered swift arrests to uproot the rebellion entirely.

sentences.zh: 水師提督黃仕簡率兵討爽文，坐逗留奪官，以命元枚，並賜孔雀翎，授參贊，趣率兵渡鹿仔港，會總督常青進討。

translations.literal: Naval Commander-in-chief Huang Shijian had led troops against Shuangwen but was stripped of office for delay; Yuanmei was appointed in his place, granted the peacock feather, made an assistant in the campaign, and urged to lead troops across at Lugang to join Governor-General Chang Qing in the advance.
translations.idiomatic: Naval commander Huang Shijian had been dismissed for delay against Shuangwen; Yuanmei replaced him, received the peacock feather and a staff role, and was urged to cross at Lugang and join governor-general Chang Qing.

sentences.zh: 六月，元枚率兵次鹿仔港，與總兵普吉保師會，即夜，師分道自柴坑仔、大武隴入，殺賊甚眾。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Yuanmei led troops to Lugang, joined forces with Commander-in-chief Pu Jibao, and that same night the armies entered by separate routes from Chaikengzi and Dawulong, killing very many rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yuanmei reached Lugang, united with commander Pu Jibao, and that night their columns entered by Chaikengzi and Dawulong, killing many rebels.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，賜雙眼孔雀翎。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the victory and awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 元枚所將止浙江兵二千，奏請益師，上命總督李侍堯發福建兵二千、廣東兵三千益元枚。

translations.literal: The troops Yuanmei commanded were only two thousand Zhejiang soldiers; he memorialized requesting reinforcements, and the emperor ordered Governor-General Li Shiyao to send two thousand Fujian troops and three thousand Guangdong troops to augment Yuanmei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmei had only two thousand Zhejiang troops; he asked for reinforcements, and the emperor ordered governor-general Li Shiyao to send two thousand from Fujian and three thousand from Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 時總兵柴大紀堅守諸羅，元枚使告大紀，期會兵攻鬥六門。

translations.literal: At that time Commander-in-chief Chai Daji was holding Zhuluo firmly; Yuanmei sent word to Daji to arrange a joint attack on Douliumen.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Chai Daji was holding Zhuluo under siege; Yuanmei sent word to coordinate a joint assault on Douliumen.

sentences.zh: 戰阿棟社，戰埤頭莊、大肚溪，屢殺賊。

translations.literal: He fought at Adongshe, fought at Pitouzhuang and Dadu Creek, and repeatedly killed rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Adongshe, Pitouzhuang, and Dadu Creek, killing rebels repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 復進攻西螺，焚條圳塘、中浦厝諸地賊莊。

translations.literal: He again advanced on Xiluo and burned rebel villages at Tiaozhuntang, Zhongpucuo, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Xiluo and burned rebel settlements at Tiaozhuntang, Zhongpucuo, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 元枚族人啟能等七十九人自賊中出，使為導。

translations.literal: Seventy-nine of Yuanmei's clansmen, including Qineng, came out from among the rebels and were made guides.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-nine of Yuanmei's kinsmen, including Qineng, escaped from rebel lines and served as guides.

sentences.zh: 元枚奏聞，並言如察出啟能等已從賊，當立誅。

translations.literal: Yuanmei reported this and also said that if investigation showed Qineng and the others had already followed the rebels, they should be executed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmei reported this and pledged that if Qineng and the others were found to have served the rebels, he would have them executed immediately.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其公當，賜緙絲蟒袍、上佩荷包，並諭：「啟能等既來歸，前此已否從賊，不須追詰。」

translations.literal: The emperor praised his impartiality, granted a brocade python robe and an imperial purse to wear, and instructed: "Since Qineng and the others have now come over, whether they followed the rebels before need not be pursued in questioning."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his fairness, gave him a brocade python robe and an imperial purse, and said: "Now that Qineng and the others have surrendered, do not investigate whether they had joined the rebels earlier."

sentences.zh: 諸羅被圍已兩月，大紀屢就告急，上屢趣元枚赴援，諭：「廷珍平硃一貴，七日而事定。

translations.literal: Zhuluo had been besieged for two months; Daji repeatedly sent urgent appeals; the emperor repeatedly urged Yuanmei to go to the relief, instructing: "Tingzhen pacified Zhu Yigui in seven days and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuluo had been under siege for two months and Daji pleaded for help repeatedly; the emperor pressed Yuanmei to relieve the city, saying: "Your grandfather Tingzhen put down Zhu Yigui in seven days.

sentences.zh: 元枚當效法其祖，毋負委任。」

translations.literal: Yuanmei should emulate his grandfather and not fail the commission entrusted to him."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmei should follow his grandfather's example and not betray the trust placed in him."

sentences.zh: 七月，元枚病作。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Yuanmei's illness came on.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yuanmei fell ill.

sentences.zh: 八月，賊自竹子腳、大肚溪、柴坑仔三道來攻。

translations.literal: In the eighth month rebels attacked from three routes: Zhuzijiao, Dadu Creek, and Chaikengzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month rebels struck from Zhuzijiao, Dadu Creek, and Chaikengzi at once.

sentences.zh: 元枚力疾出戰，病益劇，越十日，卒於軍，贈太子太保，發白金千兩治喪，賜祭葬，諡襄毅。

translations.literal: Yuanmei forced himself out to battle despite illness; his sickness grew worse, and after ten days he died in camp; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, one thousand taels of silver were issued for funeral expenses, imperial sacrifices and burial were granted, and his posthumous title was Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmei dragged himself into battle despite fever; ten days later he died in camp. He was posthumously made grand guardian of the heir apparent, given a thousand taels for his funeral, granted state burial rites, and honored as Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 元枚諡同廷珍，時稱小襄毅以別之。

translations.literal: Yuanmei's posthumous title was the same as Tingzhen's, and at the time he was called "Little Xiangyi" to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name matched his grandfather's, and contemporaries called him "Little Xiangyi" to distinguish the two.

sentences.zh: 蔡攀龍，福建同安人。

translations.literal: Cai Panlong was a native of Tong'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Panlong was from Tong'an in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 自行伍屢遷至福建澎湖右營游擊。

translations.literal: From the ranks he rose in succession to Guerrilla Commander of the Right Camp at Penghu in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to guerrilla commander of the Fujian Penghu right camp.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十一年，林爽文為亂，巡撫徐嗣曾檄詣軍。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Qianlong, when Lin Shuangwen rebelled, Governor Xu Siceng ordered him by dispatch to join the army.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 51 (1786), when Lin Shuangwen rebelled, governor Xu Siceng summoned him to the front.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，賊破鳳山，總兵柴大紀令督兵捕治。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year rebels took Fengshan; Commander-in-chief Chai Daji ordered him to direct troops in pursuit and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 52 (1787) rebels captured Fengshan, and commander Chai Daji ordered him to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 賊攻台灣府城，攀龍出戰，屢破賊。

translations.literal: When rebels attacked the Taiwan prefectural city, Panlong went out to battle and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels assaulted the Taiwan prefectural seat, Panlong took the field and beat them back repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 賊屯西園莊，攀龍率諸將瑚圖裡、丁朝雄分道攻之，殺賊三百。

translations.literal: Rebels encamped at Xiyuanzhuang; Panlong led the generals Hutuli and Ding Chaoxiong in separate attacks and killed three hundred rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held Xiyuanzhuang; Panlong led Hutuli and Ding Chaoxiong in a pincer attack that killed three hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊復攻府城，總督常青令攀龍率諸將孫全謀​​、黃像新等禦戰。

translations.literal: Rebels again attacked the prefectural city; Governor-General Chang Qing ordered Panlong to lead the generals Sun Quanmou, Huang Xiangxin, and others in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels attacked the prefectural seat again, governor-general Chang Qing ordered Panlong to lead Sun Quanmou, Huang Xiangxin, and others in the defense.

sentences.zh: 賊乘東、南二門，攀龍等力戰，殺賊數百，奪九節砲。

translations.literal: The rebels took advantage of the eastern and southern gates; Panlong and others fought with all their strength, killed several hundred rebels, and seized a nine-section cannon.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels stormed the eastern and southern gates; Panlong and his men fought fiercely, killing several hundred rebels and capturing a nine-section cannon.

sentences.zh: 論功，擢北路協副將，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In assessing merit, he was promoted to deputy commander of the northern-route brigade and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: For his merits he was promoted to deputy commander of the northern-route brigade and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 賊復至，攀龍督戰，复殺賊三百餘，予強勝巴圖魯名號。

translations.literal: The rebels came again; Panlong directed the battle and again killed more than three hundred rebels, and was given the title Qiangsheng Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels returned, Panlong directed the fighting and killed another three hundred-odd rebels; he was granted the title Qiangsheng Batulu.

sentences.zh: 七月，常青令攀龍援柴大紀諸羅，上命授海壇鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Chang Qing ordered Panlong to reinforce Chai Daji at Zhuluo, and the emperor ordered him appointed commander of the Haizhen garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Chang Qing ordered Panlong to relieve Chai Daji at Zhuluo, and the throne appointed him commander of the Haizhen garrison.

sentences.zh: 攀龍師至鹽水港，分八隊以進。

translations.literal: Panlong's army reached Yanshui Harbor and divided into eight columns to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong's force reached Yanshui Harbor and advanced in eight columns.

sentences.zh: 雨大至，賊乘雨合圍，諸將貴林、楊起麟、杭富皆戰死。

translations.literal: Great rain came; the rebels used the rain to encircle them, and the generals Gui Lin, Yang Qilin, and Hang Fu all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain fell, and the rebels used it to surround them; generals Gui Lin, Yang Qilin, and Hang Fu were all killed in action.

sentences.zh: 會大紀以師來迎，攀龍及全謀兵不及千人，偕運餉民三千人入諸羅，復出城殺賊。

translations.literal: Just then Daji came with the army to meet them; Panlong and Sun Quanmou had troops numbering less than a thousand; together with three thousand men transporting provisions they entered Zhuluo, then again went out of the city to kill rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Daji then arrived with his army to meet them. Panlong and Sun Quanmou had fewer than a thousand troops; they entered Zhuluo with three thousand supply carriers and then sallied out again to attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 總督李侍堯聞攀龍兵達諸羅，未知貴林等戰死狀，謂諸羅圍已解，入告。

translations.literal: Governor-General Li Shiyao heard that Panlong's troops had reached Zhuluo, did not know the situation of Gui Lin and others' deaths in battle, said the siege of Zhuluo was already lifted, and reported inward.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Li Shiyao, hearing that Panlong's troops had reached Zhuluo and unaware that Gui Lin and the others had been killed, reported that the siege of Zhuluo was already broken.

sentences.zh: 上擢攀龍陸路提督，參贊軍務，貴林、起麟、全謀並遷官。

translations.literal: The emperor promoted Panlong to land-forces commander-in-chief with a staff role in the campaign; Gui Lin, Qilin, and Quanmou were all also advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promoted Panlong to land-forces commander with a commission to assist in military affairs, and also advanced Gui Lin, Qilin, and Quanmou.

sentences.zh: 俄，侍堯复疏陳，上命卹戰死諸將。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Shiyao again submitted a memorial stating the facts, and the emperor ordered condolences for the generals who died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shiyao submitted another memorial clarifying the facts, and the emperor ordered posthumous honors for the fallen generals.

sentences.zh: 福康安既解嘉義圍，疏劾大紀，因言攀龍軍嘉義西門外，並無出城殺賊事，自請奪職。

translations.literal: After Fuk'anggan had relieved the siege of Jiayi, he memorialized to impeach Chai Daji, further stating that Panlong's army at the west gate outside Jiayi had no instance of going out of the city to kill rebels, and requested himself to be stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: After Fuk'anggan lifted the siege of Jiayi, he memorialized against Chai Daji, adding that Panlong's troops at Jiayi's west gate had never sallied forth to fight the rebels—and Panlong asked to be dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 擬請令還海壇本任。

translations.literal: It was proposed to order him to return to his original post at Haitan.
translations.idiomatic: The court proposed sending him back to his former post as commander of the Haizhen garrison.

sentences.zh: 上謂攀龍屢戰有功，其過尚可寬。

translations.literal: The emperor said Panlong had repeatedly fought with merit; his faults could still be treated leniently.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said Panlong had fought often and well; his faults might yet be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，逮大紀治罪，移攀龍水師提督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, Chai Daji was arrested and punished; Panlong was transferred to naval commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year, Chai Daji was arrested and punished, and Panlong was made naval commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 師攻大武隴，令攀龍駐灣里溪。

translations.literal: The army attacked Dawulong; Panlong was ordered to station at Wanlixi.
translations.idiomatic: As the army moved on Dawulong, Panlong was posted at Wanlixi.

sentences.zh: 爽文既擒，其弟勇及賊渠莊大田猶窺伺府城，攻灣里溪，圖斷府城道。

translations.literal: Shuangwen having already been captured, his younger brother Yong and the rebel leader Zhuang Datian still watched for an opportunity at the prefectural city, attacked Wanlixi, and intended to cut the road to the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shuangwen was already taken, his brother Yong and the rebel chieftain Zhuang Datian still eyed the prefectural seat, struck Wanlixi, and sought to sever the route to the city.

sentences.zh: 福康安遣攀龍分道進攻，頗有斬獲。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan sent Panlong to advance by separate routes; there were considerable kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan sent Panlong in divided columns; the fighting yielded many kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 事平，圖形紫光閣，列前二十功臣，上自為贊，許為台灣戰將中巨擘。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Glories, ranked among the foremost twenty meritorious officials; the emperor himself composed an encomium, acknowledging him as a towering figure among Taiwan's fighting generals.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was won, his likeness entered the Hall of Purple Glories among the top twenty honorees; the emperor wrote the inscription himself, calling him the greatest fighting captain Taiwan had produced.

sentences.zh: 師還，諸將言攀龍平庸，福康安亦言未能勝任，左遷江南狼山鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the various generals said Panlong was mediocre; Fuk'anggan also said he was unable to fill the post, and he was demoted to garrison commander at Langshan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, fellow commanders called Panlong unremarkable; Fuk'anggan agreed he was not equal to the job, and he was demoted to garrison commander at Langshan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Jiaqing reign.

sentences.zh: 梁朝桂，甘肅中衛人。

translations.literal: Liang Chaogui was a native of Zhongwei in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chaogui was from Zhongwei in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年，以中衛營外委從征金川，先後攻克路頂宗、布朗郭宗及功噶爾拉、丫口、昔嶺、阿喀木雅。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong, as an outer delegate of the Zhongwei battalion he followed the campaign against Jinchuan, and successively captured Ludingzong, Bulanguozong, Gongga'erla, Yakou, Xiling, and Akemuya.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 37 he joined the Jinchuan campaign as an outer delegate of the Zhongwei battalion and successively took Ludingzong, Bulanguozong, Gongga'erla, Yakou, Xiling, and Akemuya.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，克淜普，進攻喇穆喇穆山梁，奪日丫口。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he captured Qinpu, advanced to attack the Lamulamu ridge, and seized Riyakou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he took Qinpu, pressed the Lamulamu ridge, and seized Riyakou.

sentences.zh: 四十年，剿勒吉爾博寨，先登被創。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he suppressed Leji'erbo stockade, was first to ascend and was wounded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he stormed Leji'erbo stockade, led the climb, and was wounded.

sentences.zh: 四月，攻木思工噶克山，潛師入，盡克其城碉，據康薩爾至丫口山。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he attacked Musigongake Mountain, sent troops in stealth, completely captured its forts and blockhouses, and held from Kangsar to Yakou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he assailed Musigongake Mountain with a hidden force, took every fort and blockhouse, and held the ground from Kangsar to Yakou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 十月，克西里山。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he captured Xili Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he took Xili Mountain.

sentences.zh: 錄功，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: His merits were recorded and he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: His service was entered on the rolls and he received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 累遷陝西潼關協副將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Tongguan garrison in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to deputy commander of the Tongguan garrison in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 金川平，列五十功臣，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: When Jinchuan was pacified he was listed among the fifty meritorious officials and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Glories.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinchuan was pacified he was named among the fifty honorees and pictured in the Hall of Purple Glories.

sentences.zh: 累遷甘肅肅州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to garrison commander of Suzhou in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to garrison commander of Suzhou in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 坐事罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was cashiered for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 復起，自福建福寧鎮移廣東高廉鎮。

translations.literal: He was reinstated, transferred from the Funing garrison in Fujian to the Gaolian garrison in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Reinstated, he moved from Funing in Fujian to Gaolian in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，台灣林爽文為亂，莊大田應之，別為南路賊。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan; Zhuang Datian responded to him and formed a separate southern rebel force.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 52 Lin Shuangwen rose in Taiwan; Zhuang Datian joined him and became the separate rebel power of the south.

sentences.zh: 朝桂率兵敗大田於蔦松，斬馘二百餘。

translations.literal: Chaogui led troops and defeated Datian at Niaosong, beheading more than two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Chaogui led his men and routed Datian at Niaosong, taking more than two hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 賊眾數千犯大營，擊卻之，斃賊三百。

translations.literal: Several thousand rebels attacked the main camp; he drove them back and killed three hundred rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When several thousand rebels struck the main camp, he beat them back and left three hundred dead.

sentences.zh: 將軍常青慮南路賊北擾諸羅，檄朝桂堵禦，連敗之南潭、中洲、十三里莊，殲數百人。

translations.literal: General Chang Qing, fearing southern rebels would harass Zhuluo from the north, ordered Chaogui to block them; he repeatedly defeated them at Nantan, Zhongzhou, and Shisanlizhuang, destroying several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the southern rebels might press north toward Zhuluo, General Chang Qing ordered Chaogui to hold them; he defeated them again and again at Nantan, Zhongzhou, and Shisanlizhuang, killing hundreds.

sentences.zh: 九月，常青移師北路剿爽文，以朝桂守台灣府城，賊來犯，擊走之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Chang Qing moved his army north to suppress Shuangwen, leaving Chaogui to guard the Taiwan prefectural city; when rebels came to attack, he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Chang Qing marched north against Shuangwen and left Chaogui to hold the prefectural city; when rebels came, Chaogui drove them away.

sentences.zh: 其冬，援參贊恆瑞於鹽水港，毀賊藔，賜號奮勇巴圖魯；

translations.literal: That winter he reinforced Grand Coordinator Hengrui at Yanshui Harbor, destroyed rebel stockades, and was granted the title Fenyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he reinforced Grand Coordinator Hengrui at Yanshui Harbor, burned rebel strongholds, and was named Fenyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 復同恆瑞自鹿仔草進剿鎮平莊，受創，力戰敗賊。

translations.literal: Again with Hengrui he advanced from Luzicao to suppress Zhenpingzhuang, was wounded, fought fiercely and defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Hengrui in a push from Luzicao on Zhenpingzhuang, was wounded, fought on, and broke the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時提督柴大紀被圍諸羅急，朝桂欲馳援，恆瑞不聽，大紀以聞，帝令將軍福康安察奏。

translations.literal: At that time Commander-in-chief Chai Daji was urgently besieged at Zhuluo; Chaogui wished to ride to the rescue but Hengrui would not listen; Daji reported it, and the emperor ordered General Fuk'anggan to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Daji was then hard pressed at Zhuluo; Chaogui wanted to ride to his relief, but Hengrui refused. Daji appealed to the throne, and the emperor told General Fuk'anggan to investigate and report.

sentences.zh: 會福康安抵鹿仔港，檄朝桂仍駐守鹽水港及鹿仔草。

translations.literal: When Fuk'anggan arrived at Lugang he ordered Chaogui to remain garrisoning Yanshui Harbor and Luzicao.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuk'anggan reached Lugang, he ordered Chaogui to keep his post at Yanshui Harbor and Luzicao.

sentences.zh: 五十三年春，就擢福建陸路提督。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifty-third year he was promptly promoted to Fujian land-forces commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qianlong 53 he was promoted on the spot to Fujian's land-forces commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 檄剿麻豆莊、大武隴屯賊，通郡城要道。

translations.literal: He was ordered to suppress rebels at Madouzhuang and the Dawulong garrison, opening the vital route to the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched against the rebels at Madouzhuang and the Dawulong garrison to reopen the main road to the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 大田時據大武隴拒守，朝桂自茅港尾繞至阿里港迎截；

translations.literal: Datian then held Dawulong in defense; Chaogui from Maogangwei circled around to Ali Harbor to intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: Datian was then holding Dawulong; Chaogui swung from Maogangwei around to Ali Harbor to cut him off.

sentences.zh: 复赴打狗、竹仔各港口截其走路。

translations.literal: Again he went to Dagou, Zhuzai, and various harbors to cut off his escape routes.
translations.idiomatic: He then sealed Dagou, Zhuzai, and the other ports to block Datian's escape.

sentences.zh: 大田力不支，自牛莊竄極南之郎嶠，負山阻海。

translations.literal: Datian could not hold out; from Niuzhuang he fled to Langqiao at the extreme south, backed by mountains and blocked by sea.
translations.idiomatic: Datian could not endure; he fled from Niuzhuang to Langqiao at the island's southern tip, with mountains at his back and sea before him.

sentences.zh: 福康安自風港進至柴城，分六隊直逼海岸，與朝桂環攻之，大田及他賊目四十餘悉就擒。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan advanced from Fenggang to Chaicheng, divided six columns to press straight to the coast, and with Chaogui besieged him from all sides; Datian and more than forty other rebel leaders were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan came up from Fenggang to Chaicheng, split six columns to drive the coast, and with Chaogui closed the ring; Datian and more than forty other rebel leaders were taken.

sentences.zh: 台灣平，再圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: Taiwan was pacified; his portrait was again placed in the Hall of Purple Glories.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwan was pacified, his likeness again entered the Hall of Purple Glories.

sentences.zh: 金門巡洋艦被劫，以朝桂不能戢盜，移廣西。

translations.literal: A patrol vessel at Kinmen was plundered; because Chaogui could not restrain pirates, he was transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A patrol vessel at Kinmen was seized by pirates; because Chaogui could not keep the sea in order, he was moved to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 再移湖廣。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 普吉保，札庫塔氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Pu Jibao, of the Jakuta clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Jibao, of the Jakuta clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十年，以藍翎侍衛從軍徵烏什，有功，補三等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Qianlong, as a bodyguard with the blue insignia he joined the army to campaign against Ush, performed meritorious service, and was appointed third-rank bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 30 he went to war against Ush as a blue-insignia bodyguard, distinguished himself, and was made a third-rank bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，從參贊大臣舒常攻日旁，有功。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he followed Grand Coordinator Shu Chang in attacking Ripang, with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he followed Grand Coordinator Shu Chang against Ripang and earned credit.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，從副將軍豐升額攻凱立葉山，進抵迪噶拉穆札山。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he followed Deputy Commander-in-chief Feng Sheng'e in attacking Kailiye Mountain, advancing to Digalamuzha Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he served under Deputy Commander Feng Sheng'e at Kailiye Mountain and pushed on to Digalamuzha Mountain.

sentences.zh: 賊分三隊，普吉保偕侍衛瑪爾占等夾攻，斃賊無算，賜衝捷巴圖魯名號。

translations.literal: The rebels divided into three columns; Pu Jibao together with bodyguards Ma'erzhan and others attacked from both flanks, killing countless rebels, and was granted the title Chongjie Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy split into three bodies, Pu Jibao and bodyguard Ma'erzhan and others struck from both flanks and killed without number; he received the title Chongjie Batulu.

sentences.zh: 四十年，攻噶爾丹寺諸地，連破木城、石碉。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he attacked Ga'erdan Monastery and other places, successively breaking wooden palisades and stone blockhouses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he fought at Ga'erdan Monastery and elsewhere, breaking wooden walls and stone blockhouses in succession.

sentences.zh: 上獎普吉保勇往，累擢福建汀州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: The emperor commended Pu Jibao's daring advance and repeatedly promoted him to garrison commander of Tingzhou in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Pu Jibao's bold advance and raised him by stages to garrison commander of Tingzhou in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 林爽文為亂，總督常青檄普吉保會剿，五十二年，率水師渡台灣，迭破賊鹿仔港、八卦山，上嘉其奮勉。

translations.literal: When Lin Shuangwen rebelled, Governor-General Chang Qing ordered Pu Jibao to join the suppression; in the fifty-second year he led the naval forces across to Taiwan, repeatedly defeating the rebels at Lugang and Baguashan; the emperor praised his zeal.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Shuangwen rebelled, Governor-General Chang Qing summoned Pu Jibao to the joint campaign; in Qianlong 52 he crossed to Taiwan at the head of the fleet, took Lugang and Baguashan in turn, and won the emperor's praise for his zeal.

sentences.zh: 爽文見師至，退守鬥六門、大里杙。

translations.literal: Shuangwen, seeing the army arrive, fell back to defend Douliumen and Daliyi.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the imperial host arrive, Shuangwen withdrew to hold Douliumen and Daliyi.

sentences.zh: 普吉保以師進，爽文攻諸羅，赴援，抵笨港，率游擊海亮等殲賊數百，毀賊莊七，得旨嘉獎，賜玉搬指、荷包、蟒袍。

translations.literal: Pu Jibao advanced with his army; Shuangwen attacked Zhuluo; he went to the rescue, reaching Bengang, leading Guerrilla Commander Hailiang and others to destroy several hundred rebels, destroying seven rebel villages; he received an imperial commendation and was granted a jade thumb ring, purse, and python robe.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Jibao pressed forward; when Shuangwen struck Zhuluo, he hurried to the relief, reached Bengang, and with guerrilla commander Hailiang and others killed hundreds of rebels and destroyed seven rebel villages. An imperial commendation followed, with a jade thumb ring, purse, and python robe.

sentences.zh: 笨港潰賊糾眾截我兵，普吉保擊斬甚眾。

translations.literal: Routed rebels at Bengang gathered a mob to intercept government troops; Pu Jibao struck and beheaded very many.
translations.idiomatic: Routed rebels at Bengang rallied to cut off the government column; Pu Jibao struck and slew a great many.

sentences.zh: 嗣以駐兵元長莊、月眉莊不進，旨嚴飭。

translations.literal: Subsequently because he stationed troops at Yuanchangzhuang and Yuemeizhuang without advancing, he received a stern imperial reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because he sat idle at Yuanchangzhuang and Yuemeizhuang, the court sent a stern rebuke.

sentences.zh: 尋攻大埔林，收復鬥六門。

translations.literal: Soon he attacked Dapulin and recovered Douliumen.
translations.idiomatic: He soon attacked Dapulin and retook Douliumen.

sentences.zh: 爽文竄內山，普吉保從諸將徒步陟山搜捕。

translations.literal: Shuangwen fled into the inner mountains; Pu Jibao followed the various generals on foot up the mountains to search and capture.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen fled into the interior hills; Pu Jibao joined the other commanders in climbing the mountains on foot to hunt him down.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，以兵扼科仔坑口，合圍，俘爽文。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, with troops he held Kezikeng Pass, joined the encirclement, and captured Shuangwen alive.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 53 he blocked Kezikeng Pass with his men, helped close the net, and took Shuangwen alive.

sentences.zh: 南路莊大田亦就擒。

translations.literal: The southern-route rebel Zhuang Datian was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Datian of the southern front was captured as well.

sentences.zh: 台灣平，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: Taiwan was pacified; his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Glories.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwan was pacified, his likeness was placed in the Hall of Purple Glories.

sentences.zh: 普吉保初克鹿仔港，以福康安疏薦，授台灣總兵。

translations.literal: When Pu Jibao first captured Lugang, on Fuk'anggan's memorial recommendation he was appointed Taiwan garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Pu Jibao's first victory at Lugang, Fuk'anggan recommended him and he was made garrison commander of Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 明年，上念台灣初定，慮普吉保不能勝，命解任。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor, reflecting that Taiwan had only just been pacified and fearing Pu Jibao could not fill the post, ordered him relieved of duty.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, mindful that Taiwan had only just been settled and doubting Pu Jibao was equal to the post, the emperor ordered him removed.

sentences.zh: 尋授廣西左江鎮，坐責把總黎振乾投水死，戍伊犁。

translations.literal: Soon appointed to the Zuojiang garrison in Guangxi; convicted for holding a platoon commander Li Zhenqian responsible when he drowned himself, and exiled to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the Zuojiang garrison in Guangxi, but was convicted after platoon commander Li Zhenqian drowned himself on his watch and was sent to exile in Yili.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 丁朝雄，字伯宜，江蘇通州人。

translations.literal: Ding Chaoxiong, courtesy name Boyi, was a native of Tongzhou in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Chaoxiong, styled Boyi, was from Tongzhou in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 自行伍累擢福建台灣水師副將。

translations.literal: Rising from the ranks he was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Taiwan naval forces in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks to become deputy commander of the Taiwan naval forces in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十一年，以任滿赴部引見，至省城，聞林爽文亂起。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Qianlong, when his term expired he went to the capital for audience; reaching the provincial capital, he heard Lin Shuangwen's rebellion had begun.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 51, as his term ended he set out for the capital for audience; at the provincial seat he learned that Lin Shuangwen had risen.

sentences.zh: 朝雄策東港與鳳山犄角，爽文所必爭，白總督常青，請兵屯東港，斷其糧道。

translations.literal: Chaoxiong strategized that Donggang and Fengshan formed a pincer Shuangwen was sure to contest; he informed Governor-General Chang Qing and asked for troops to garrison Donggang and cut his supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoxiong argued that Donggang and Fengshan formed a pincer Shuangwen was bound to fight for, told Governor-General Chang Qing so, and asked for troops at Donggang to sever the rebels' grain route.

sentences.zh: 常青不能用，遣朝雄還台灣，佐海壇鎮總兵郝壯猷討爽文。

translations.literal: Chang Qing could not adopt it; he sent Chaoxiong back to Taiwan to assist Haizhen garrison commander Hao Zhuangyou in suppressing Shuangwen.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Qing would not heed him and sent Chaoxiong back to Taiwan to serve under Haizhen garrison commander Hao Zhuangyou against Shuangwen.

sentences.zh: 五十二年春，壯猷偕朝雄率兵二千餘擊賊，馘三百，俘二十五。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifty-second year Zhuangyou together with Chaoxiong led more than two thousand troops to attack rebels, taking three hundred heads and twenty-five prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qianlong 52 Zhuangyou and Chaoxiong led a little over two thousand men against the rebels, taking three hundred heads and twenty-five prisoners.

sentences.zh: 日將暮，賊復來攻，朝雄复殺賊百餘，賊始去。

translations.literal: As day was about to set rebels again attacked; Chaoxiong again killed over a hundred rebels before the rebels finally withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: As dusk neared the rebels came again; Chaoxiong killed another hundred-odd before they at last withdrew.

sentences.zh: 攻鳳山，朝雄乘東門，首諸軍入，鳳山遂復。

translations.literal: Attacking Fengshan, Chaoxiong scaled the east gate, first of the armies to enter; Fengshan was thus recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Fengshan, Chaoxiong went over the east gate ahead of the host; Fengshan was recovered.

sentences.zh: 黃仕簡檄朝雄守安平海口。

translations.literal: Huang Shijian ordered Chaoxiong to guard Anping seaport.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shijian ordered Chaoxiong to hold Anping harbor.

sentences.zh: 賊攻府城，朝雄偕知府楊廷樺督兵民力禦。

translations.literal: Rebels attacked the prefectural city; Chaoxiong together with Prefect Yang Tinghua directed troops and civilians to resist with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels struck the prefectural city, Chaoxiong and Prefect Yang Tinghua rallied troops and townspeople to defend it with all they had.

sentences.zh: 賊攻桶盤棧，朝雄為前鋒，出戰，台灣道永福、同知楊廷理率兵民繼，复殺賊百餘，賊敗走。

translations.literal: Rebels attacked Tongpanzhan; Chaoxiong as vanguard went out to fight; Taiwan Circuit Intendant Yongfu and Subprefect Yang Tingli led troops and civilians in support, again killing over a hundred rebels; the rebels were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongpanzhan Chaoxiong led the van in a sortie; Intendant Yongfu and Subprefect Yang Tingli followed with soldiers and militia, cut down another hundred-odd rebels, and put the enemy to flight.

sentences.zh: 冬，朝雄偕游擊倪賓率兵千二百、義民二千餘攻東港。

translations.literal: That winter Chaoxiong with Guerrilla Commander Ni Bin led twelve hundred troops and over two thousand local militia to attack Donggang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Chaoxiong and guerrilla commander Ni Bin took twelve hundred regulars and more than two thousand militiamen against Donggang.

sentences.zh: 東港賊數万，其渠吳豹以海岸淺，度舟不能至，不為備。

translations.literal: Donggang rebels numbered tens of thousands; their leader Wu Bao, judging the coast shallow and estimating boats could not approach, made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of rebels held Donggang; their chief Wu Bao, thinking the shore too shallow for boats, made no ready defense.

sentences.zh: 朝雄遣諜以水注賊砲，乘雨至水漲，遣兵民分道登岸殺賊，俘豹。

translations.literal: Chaoxiong sent spies to flood the rebels' cannon with water; taking advantage of rain until the water rose, he sent troops and civilians by separate routes ashore to kill rebels and captured Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoxiong sent agents to flood the enemy guns with water; when rain swelled the tide he landed men and militia by separate paths, cut down the rebels, and took Bao.

sentences.zh: 以兵寡不能克，報常青請益兵。

translations.literal: Because his forces were few and he could not overcome them, he reported to Chang Qing requesting more troops.
translations.idiomatic: Too few to finish the fight, he reported to Chang Qing for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 常青令駐港口護餉道。

translations.literal: Chang Qing ordered him to station at the harbor protecting the grain supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Qing told him to hold the harbor and guard the grain route.

sentences.zh: 既，令攻竹仔港，毀賊舟。

translations.literal: Subsequently he ordered him to attack Zhuzai Harbor and destroy rebel boats.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered to strike Zhuzai Harbor and burn the rebel boats.

sentences.zh: 五十三年春，復攻東港，仍遣諜以水注賊砲，督兵攻渡口，賊驚竄，逐三十餘裡，乃倚山而軍。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifty-third year he again attacked Donggang, again sending spies to flood the rebels' cannon with water, directing troops to attack the crossing; rebels fled in alarm; he pursued over thirty li, then encamped backed by mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qianlong 53 he attacked Donggang again, again flooding the enemy guns by stratagem, stormed the ford, and chased the fleeing rebels more than thirty li before making camp against the hills.

sentences.zh: 賊夜來犯，朝雄戒勿動；

translations.literal: Rebels came to attack by night; Chaoxiong warned troops not to move.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came by night; Chaoxiong ordered his men to hold still.

sentences.zh: 及曉，賊倦，掩擊，大破之。

translations.literal: At dawn, when the rebels were weary, he made a surprise attack and routed them decisively.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak, when the enemy was spent, he fell on them from cover and broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 爽文遣其徒來援，朝雄築壘困之。

translations.literal: Shuangwen sent his followers to reinforce; Chaoxiong built stockades to hem them in.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen sent men to relieve them; Chaoxiong threw up stockades to pin them down.

sentences.zh: 賊潰圍出，設伏斷其歸路，而自將追之，大破賊，遂復東港。

translations.literal: Rebels broke out of the encirclement; he set an ambush to cut their return route and himself led the pursuit, routing the rebels decisively, and thus recovered Donggang.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels burst out, he laid an ambush across their retreat and led the pursuit himself, shattering them and retaking Donggang.

sentences.zh: 福康安上其功，授海壇鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan reported his merit; he was appointed garrison commander of Haizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan memorialized his merit, and he was made garrison commander of Haizhen.

sentences.zh: 既，福康安劾柴大紀受陋規，言朝雄為安平協副將時亦有此，當奪職戍軍台，上以朝雄攻東港戰有功，命留任。

translations.literal: Subsequently Fuk'anggan impeached Chai Daji for accepting shabby bribes, saying Chaoxiong when deputy commander at Anping had done the same and ought to be stripped of office and exiled to the military penal colony; the emperor, because Chaoxiong's fighting at Donggang had merit, ordered him to remain in post.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fuk'anggan impeached Chai Daji for taking mean bribes and said Chaoxiong had done the same as Anping's deputy commander and should be dismissed and sent to the military penal colony; the emperor, weighing his service at Donggang, let him keep his post.

sentences.zh: 林鬎舵、林明灼者，海盜渠也，五十四年，朝雄巡洋至汜澳，破盜巢，得鬎舵等；

translations.literal: Lin Liguduo and Lin Mingzhuo were pirate chieftains; in the fifty-fourth year Chaoxiong on patrol reached Fan'ao, broke their pirate nest and captured Liguduo and others.
translations.idiomatic: The pirate chiefs Lin Liguduo and Lin Mingzhuo were broken when Chaoxiong, patrolling in Qianlong 54, raided their nest at Fan'ao and took Liguduo and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 而明灼拒殺參將張殿魁。

translations.literal: But Mingzhuo resisted and killed Lieutenant Commander Zhang Diankui.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhuo, however, resisted and killed lieutenant commander Zhang Diankui.

sentences.zh: 上責總督伍拉納，伍拉納以屬朝雄，督舟師出海，遇諸大麥洋，俟其近，發大砲，斃數酋，明灼窮蹙，躍入海，官軍鉤致，俘以歸。

translations.literal: The emperor reprimanded Governor-General Wulana; Wulana turned the matter over to Chaoxiong, who directed the naval force to sea; encountering them at Zhudamaiyang, he waited until they drew near, fired great cannon, killed several chieftains; Mingzhuo, cornered, leaped into the sea; government troops hooked him up and brought him back prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Governor-General Wulana, who handed the hunt to Chaoxiong; Chaoxiong put the fleet to sea, met the pirates at Zhudamaiyang, waited until they were close, and opened with heavy guns, killing several chiefs; Mingzhuo, trapped, leapt into the water, was gaffed up by government sailors, and brought in alive.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，追論朝雄在台灣失察天地會邪教，當奪職；

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, retrospectively it was adjudged that Chaoxiong in Taiwan had failed to detect the Heaven and Earth Society heterodox cult and ought to be stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 55 he was judged retrospectively for failing in Taiwan to detect the Heaven and Earth Society secret society and was to be dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 上諮伍拉納朝雄在官狀，伍拉納言朝雄督水師捕盜有勞，命還任。

translations.literal: The emperor inquired of Wulana about Chaoxiong's conduct in office; Wulana said Chaoxiong had merit in supervising the naval forces to capture bandits, and he was ordered to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Governor-General Wulana about Ding Chaoxiong's performance in office. Wulana reported that Chaoxiong had distinguished himself directing the navy in the pursuit of pirates, and the court ordered him restored to his post.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，攝水師提督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, he acted as naval commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 58 he served as acting naval commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，入覲，至清江浦，病篤。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he came to audience; reaching Qingjiangpu, his illness became grave.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 59 he traveled to court for audience, but upon reaching Qingjiangpu his illness turned critical.

sentences.zh: 乞罷歸，卒於上海舟中。

translations.literal: He begged to resign and return; he died in a boat at Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to resign and return home, and died aboard his boat at Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 鄂輝，碧魯氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: E Hui, of the Bilu clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: E Hui, of the Bilu clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 自前鋒分發四川試用守備。

translations.literal: From the Vanguard he was assigned to Sichuan as a probationary garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Posted from the Vanguard, he was sent to Sichuan as a probationary garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 七遷建昌鎮總兵。

translations.literal: After seven promotions he became commander of the Jianchang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After seven promotions he rose to commander of the Jianchang garrison.

sentences.zh: 從大學士阿桂定蘭州回亂，予法什尚阿巴圖魯名號。

translations.literal: He followed Grand Secretary Agui in pacifying the Lanzhou Muslim rebellion and was given the title Fashishang Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand Secretary Agui in suppressing the Muslim uprising at Lanzhou and was granted the honorific title Fashishang Batulu.

sentences.zh: 再遷成都將軍。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to general at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to general at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十二年，署四川總督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of Qianlong he acted as Governor-General of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 52 he served as acting governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 將軍福康安討台灣亂民林爽文，上命鄂輝率四川屯練降番濟師。

translations.literal: When General Fuk'anggan campaigned against the Taiwan rebel Lin Shuangwen, the emperor ordered E Hui to lead Sichuan militia, trained troops, and surrendered tribesmen to reinforce the army.
translations.idiomatic: When General Fuk'anggan marched against the Taiwan rebel Lin Shuangwen, the emperor ordered E Hui to lead Sichuan militia, trained levies, and surrendered tribal auxiliaries to reinforce the campaign.

sentences.zh: 尋授參贊，從渡海援嘉義。

translations.literal: Soon he was made a staff deputy and crossed the sea to relieve Jiayi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed campaign deputy and crossed the strait to relieve Jiayi.

sentences.zh: 鄂輝屯東莊溪橋，攻克牛稠山竹柵，嘉義圍解。

translations.literal: E Hui encamped at Dongzhuangxi Bridge, captured the bamboo stockade at Niuchoushan, and the siege of Jiayi was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: E Hui encamped at Dongzhuangxi Bridge, stormed the bamboo stockade at Niuchoushan, and the siege of Jiayi was broken.

sentences.zh: 逐賊至大排竹，殲之。

translations.literal: He pursued the rebels to Dapaizhu and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: He drove the rebels to Dapaizhu and destroyed them there.

sentences.zh: 師攻鬥六門，賊自山下撲，鄂輝督兵衝截，賊奔逸，攻克大埔林、大埔尾二莊，賊潰。

translations.literal: When the army attacked Douliumen the rebels rushed down from the hills; E Hui directed troops to charge and intercept, the rebels fled, and Dapulin and Dapowei were taken and the rebels collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Douliumen the rebels charged down from the hills; E Hui led his men in a countercharge, broke their attack, and seized the villages of Dapulin and Dapowei as the enemy scattered in rout.

sentences.zh: 爽文自所居大里杙奔內山番界，鄂輝逐之至集埔。

translations.literal: Shuangwen fled from his residence at Daliyi into the mountain aborigine territory; E Hui pursued him to Jipu.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen fled his stronghold at Daliyi into the inner mountain aboriginal lands, and E Hui pursued him as far as Jipu.

sentences.zh: 五十三年春，诇知爽文所匿地曰東勢角，福康安督鄂輝及舒亮追捕，自歸仔頭至麻著社，分軍，鄂輝自撲仔離東山路進，舒亮直取東勢角。

translations.literal: In spring of the fifty-third year scouts learned Shuangwen was hiding at Dongshijiao; Fuk'anggan directed E Hui and Shu Liang in pursuit from Guizaitou to Mazheshe, dividing the army—E Hui advanced by the eastern route from Puzaili, Shu Liang struck directly for Dongshijiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qianlong 53, intelligence placed Shuangwen at Dongshijiao. Fuk'anggan directed E Hui and Shu Liang in pursuit from Guizaitou to Mazheshe, splitting their forces: E Hui would advance along the eastern road from Puzaili, while Shu Liang would strike Dongshijiao head-on.

sentences.zh: 是役遂俘爽文，亂乃定。

translations.literal: In this campaign Shuangwen was captured and the rebellion was settled.
translations.idiomatic: In that operation Shuangwen was taken prisoner, and the rebellion was finally brought to an end.

sentences.zh: 上命台灣嘉義立諸將帥生祠，鄂輝與焉。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered living shrines erected at Jiayi in Taiwan to the generals, and E Hui was among them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered living shrines erected at Jiayi in Taiwan to honor the commanding generals, and E Hui was numbered among them.

sentences.zh: 師還，圖形紫光閣，賜雙眼孔雀翎、雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: When the army returned, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Glories; he was granted the double-eyed peacock feather and a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return his portrait was hung in the Hall of Purple Glories, and he received the double-eyed peacock feather together with a hereditary Cloud Cavalry captaincy.

sentences.zh: 鄂輝朝熱河行在。

translations.literal: E Hui attended the emperor at the Rehe traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: E Hui presented himself to the emperor at the traveling palace in Rehe.

sentences.zh: 廓爾喀侵西藏，據濟嚨、聶拉木諸地。

translations.literal: The Gurkhas invaded Tibet and seized Gyirong, Nyalam, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: The Gurkhas invaded Tibet and occupied Gyirong, Nyalam, and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 上促鄂輝還四川，與提督成德帥師赴援，又命侍郎巴忠往按。

translations.literal: The emperor urged E Hui back to Sichuan to join Commander-in-chief Cheng De in leading relief forces, and also sent Vice Minister Ba Zhong to investigate on site.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed E Hui to return to Sichuan and, together with commander Cheng De, lead a relief force into Tibet, while also dispatching Vice Minister Ba Zhong to conduct an on-site investigation.

sentences.zh: 巴忠先嘗為駐藏大臣，習藏事，示意噶布倫，令賂廓爾喀返侵地。

translations.literal: Ba Zhong had previously served as Resident Commissioner in Tibet and knew Tibetan affairs; he signaled the kalöns to bribe the Gurkhas to return the seized territory.
translations.idiomatic: Ba Zhong had once served as the Qing resident commissioner in Tibet and knew Tibetan affairs well; he quietly instructed the kalöns to buy off the Gurkhas and recover the lost territory.

sentences.zh: 鄂輝等遂與議和，疏陳善後事。

translations.literal: E Hui and others thereupon made peace and memorialized on measures for aftermath.
translations.idiomatic: E Hui and his colleagues thereupon negotiated a settlement and submitted a memorial outlining measures for the aftermath.

sentences.zh: 尋授四川總督。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed Governor-General of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，廓爾喀渝盟，复侵濟嚨、聶拉木諸地。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year the Gurkhas broke the treaty and again invaded Gyirong, Nyalam, and neighboring areas.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 56 the Gurkhas violated the agreement and again invaded Gyirong, Nyalam, and the surrounding region.

sentences.zh: 上命將軍福康安督師討廓爾喀，責鄂輝誤用巴忠議致復生事，奪官，予副都統銜駐藏，聽福康安指揮，福康安令督餉。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered General Fuk'anggan to command the campaign against the Gurkhas, blamed E Hui for wrongly adopting Ba Zhong's plan and causing renewed trouble, stripped his office, gave him vice banner commander rank to remain in Tibet under Fuk'anggan's orders, and Fuk'anggan put him in charge of supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor placed General Fuk'anggan in overall command of the campaign against the Gurkhas, held E Hui responsible for having followed Ba Zhong's counsel and thereby inviting a renewed crisis, stripped him of office, and assigned him to Tibet with the rank of vice banner commander under Fuk'anggan's command; Fuk'anggan then put him in charge of provisioning the army.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書和琳劾鄂輝得廓爾喀貢表不以上聞，命奪副都統銜，逮赴前藏荷校示罰。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Helin impeached E Hui for receiving Gurkha tribute memorials without reporting them; he was stripped of vice banner commander rank and arrested to front Tibet to bear the cangue as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Helin impeached E Hui for having received Gurkha tribute memorials without reporting them to the throne. He was stripped of his vice banner commander rank, arrested, and sent to front Tibet to bear the cangue as a public punishment.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，命還京師，授拜唐阿。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he was ordered back to the capital and appointed a Baitangga guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 58 he was recalled to the capital and appointed a Baitangga guardsman.

sentences.zh: 加員外郎銜，遷熱河總管。

translations.literal: He received the additional title of vice director and was transferred to superintendent of Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional rank of vice director and transferred to superintendent of Rehe.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，命以侍衛詣荊州從剿教匪，戰有功，以都統銜加太子少保，授湖南提督。

translations.literal: At the start of Jiaqing he was sent as a guard to Jingzhou to join the suppression of sectarian rebels, fought with merit, and with banner commander rank plus Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent was made Commander-in-chief of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiaqing reign he was ordered to Jingzhou as an imperial guardsman to join the campaign against the sectarian rebels. After distinguished service he was promoted to banner commander with the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and appointed commander of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 屢破賊，與額勒登保等攻克石隆山，斬賊渠石柳鄧，封三等男。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated rebels, with Erlaedengbao and others took Shilong Mountain, beheaded the rebel chief Shi Liudeng, and was enfeoffed as third-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly defeated rebel bands and, together with Erlaedengbao and others, stormed Shilong Mountain, beheaded the rebel chieftain Shi Liudeng, and was enfeoffed as a third-class baron.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the reign he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，諡恪靖，祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, posthumous title Kejing, and was honored in the Shrine of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died. He was granted the posthumous title Kejing and entered for worship in the Shrine of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 四年，追論在湖北軍中受餽白金四千，罷祀。
