translations.literal: In the fourth year a retrospective inquiry found he had accepted four thousand taels of silver while in the Hubei army, and his shrine worship was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year a retrospective review found that while serving in the Hubei theater he had accepted four thousand taels in silver gifts, and his place in the shrine was revoked.

sentences.zh: 舒亮，蘇佳氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Shu Liang, of the Suja clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Liang, of the Suja clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 自前鋒累遷參領。

translations.literal: From the Vanguard he rose by stages to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Starting in the Vanguard, he rose through successive promotions to company commander.

sentences.zh: 師徵金川，舒亮從副都統齊里克齊率健銳營為裨將。

translations.literal: On the Jinchuan campaign Shu Liang followed Vice Banner Commander Qilikichi leading the Elite Vanguard Camp as deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinchuan campaign Shu Liang served under Vice Banner Commander Qilikichi, leading the Elite Vanguard Battalion as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 攻穆谷，舒亮伏山下待賊，殺賊甚眾。

translations.literal: At the assault on Mugou Shu Liang lay in ambush below the mountain waiting for the enemy and killed a great many.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Mugou, Shu Liang lay in ambush below the slope and waited for the enemy to pass; when they did, he cut down a great many of them.

sentences.zh: 攻卡角，賊匿山溝，舒亮於密箐中望見火光，以火器就擊之，賊驚潰。

translations.literal: At Kajiao the rebels hid in a mountain ravine; Shu Liang spied firelight in a dense thicket and fired upon it with firearms; the rebels fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Kajiao the rebels concealed themselves in a mountain ravine. Shu Liang caught the glow of their fires through a dense thicket and brought firearms to bear on the spot; the rebels broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 以功，累遷鑲黃旗滿洲副都統。

translations.literal: For merit he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Banner Commander of the Bordered Yellow Manchu Banner.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was repeatedly promoted until he held the post of vice banner commander of the Bordered Yellow Manchu Banner.

sentences.zh: 從克噶拉依，賜穆騰額巴圖魯名號。

translations.literal: He followed the capture of Garayi and was granted the title Muteng'e Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Garayi and was granted the honorific title Muteng'e Batulu.

sentences.zh: 師還，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: When the army returned, his portrait entered the Hall of Purple Glories.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, his portrait was added to the Hall of Purple Glories.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十六年，大學士阿桂討撒拉爾亂回蘇四十三，舒亮從。

translations.literal: In Qianlong year forty-six Grand Secretary Agui campaigned against the Salar rebel Muslim Su Forty-three, and Shu Liang followed.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 46, Grand Secretary Agui marched against the Salar rebel Su Forty-three, and Shu Liang accompanied the expedition.

sentences.zh: 初至，破賊華林山。

translations.literal: Upon first arrival they defeated the rebels at Hualin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On first contact the force routed the rebels on Hualin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 賊掘濠設卡以自固。

translations.literal: The rebels dug trenches and set stockades to fortify themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dug moats and threw up stockades to hold their ground.

sentences.zh: 阿桂令海蘭察自山西攻賊卡，舒亮自南山進，當賊鋒，賊競出，射舒亮，傷左股，舒亮拔箭裹創，复戰，奪賊卡四，殺賊百餘。

translations.literal: Agui ordered Hailancha to attack rebel stockades from the west while Shu Liang advanced from the south mountain to meet the enemy vanguard; rebels swarmed out and shot Shu Liang, wounding his left thigh; he pulled out the arrow, bandaged the wound, fought again, took four rebel stockades, and killed over a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Agui ordered Hailancha to strike the rebel stockades from the west while Shu Liang advanced from the southern heights to take the enemy's front. The rebels poured out to meet him and shot Shu Liang through the left thigh. He pulled out the arrow, bound the wound, and went back into the fight, capturing four stockades and killing more than a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 又與海蘭察诇賊不備，以土囊填濠渡軍，殲守濠賊，复奪十餘卡。

translations.literal: Again with Hailancha he spied when the enemy were off guard, filled the trenches with earth bags to cross troops, wiped out trench defenders, and retook over ten stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Again joining Hailancha, he caught the enemy off guard, filled the moats with earth-filled sacks to bring troops across, annihilated the defenders in the trenches, and recaptured more than ten stockades.

sentences.zh: 蘇四十三既誅，复剿華林寺餘匪。

translations.literal: After Su Forty-three was executed they again suppressed remnant bandits at Hualin Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Forty-three was put to death, the army turned to mop up the remaining bandits at Hualin Temple.

sentences.zh: 事平，還京師。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled they returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign was concluded, they returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 林爽文之亂，福康安出視師，舒亮以正黃旗護軍統領為領隊大臣。

translations.literal: During Lin Shuangwen's rebellion Fuk'anggan took field command; Shu Liang served as expedition commissioner in his capacity as colonel of the Plain Yellow Banner Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Lin Shuangwen's rebellion Fuk'anggan took personal command in the field, and Shu Liang accompanied him as expedition commissioner while serving as colonel of the Plain Yellow Banner Guard.

sentences.zh: 至台灣，福康安軍道笨港救嘉義，令舒亮出別道分賊勢。

translations.literal: Reaching Taiwan, Fuk'anggan led the army via Bengang to relieve Jiayi and ordered Shu Liang out on a separate route to divide rebel strength.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Taiwan, Fuk'anggan led the main force along the Bengang route to relieve Jiayi and ordered Shu Liang to move by a separate road so as to divide the rebel strength.

sentences.zh: 賊方據北大肚山拒我，舒亮迎擊，敗之，連破南大肚、王田、瀨湑、半山、坑子諸莊，遂克烏日莊。

translations.literal: Rebels held Beidatushan to block the advance; Shu Liang met them in battle, defeated them, and in succession took Nandadu, Wangtian, Laiyu, Banshan, Kengzi and other villages, finally capturing Wuri Village.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were holding Beidatushan to block the advance; Shu Liang met them in battle, broke their line, and in succession overran the villages of Nandadu, Wangtian, Laiyu, Banshan, Kengzi, and others, until at last he took Wuri Village.

sentences.zh: 會福康安軍夾擊，解嘉義圍。

translations.literal: Joining Fuk'anggan's forces in a pincer, the siege of Jiayi was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Coordinating with Fuk'anggan's main column in a pincer attack, he helped lift the siege of Jiayi.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，爽文竄匿東勢角。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year Shuangwen lurked at Dongshijiao.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 53 Shuangwen was hiding out at Dongshijiao.

sentences.zh: 福康安督舒亮等追逮，令舒亮直取東勢角，山徑峻險，將卒皆步上，殺賊二千餘。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan directed Shu Liang and others in pursuit, ordering Shu Liang to strike Dongshijiao directly; the mountain paths were steep and perilous, officers and men all climbed on foot, and killed over two thousand rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan directed Shu Liang and the others in pursuit and ordered Shu Liang to take Dongshijiao by a direct assault. The mountain paths were steep and treacherous, and officers and men alike had to climb on foot; in the fighting they killed more than two thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 爽文复走老衢峙，舒亮督諸軍急進，獲之，亂遂定。

translations.literal: Shuangwen fled again to Laoquzhi; Shu Liang urged the armies forward in haste, captured him, and the rebellion was finally settled.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen fled again toward Laoquzhi. Shu Liang pressed the columns forward without pause, captured him, and the rebellion was at last settled.

sentences.zh: 上以台灣遠在海外，主客民雜處，風俗素悍，命於府城及嘉義立諸將帥生祠，示威德。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering Taiwan distant overseas with mixed indigenous and settler populations and notoriously fierce customs, ordered living shrines to the generals at the prefectural seat and Jiayi to display imperial might and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, reflecting that Taiwan lay far across the sea, that settlers and indigenous peoples were intermixed, and that local customs had long been fierce, ordered living shrines to the campaigning generals erected at the prefectural seat and at Jiayi, so that imperial authority and benevolence might be made visible.

sentences.zh: 祠成，命並及在事疆吏，首福康安，次海蘭察、李侍堯、普爾普、鄂輝、徐嗣曾，而以舒亮殿焉。

translations.literal: When the shrines were completed he ordered provincial officials involved included as well: first Fuk'anggan, then Hailancha, Li Shiyao, Pulupu, E Hui, Xu Siceng, with Shu Liang listed last.
translations.idiomatic: When the shrines were completed, he also ordered that provincial officials who had taken part in the campaign be included: Fuk'anggan first, then Hailancha, Li Shiyao, Pulupu, E Hui, and Xu Siceng, with Shu Liang placed last in the roll of honor.

sentences.zh: 尋授鑲紅旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed Mongol banner commander of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Mongol banner commander of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 師還，命監爽文及其徒賴大等生致京師。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was ordered to escort Shuangwen and his follower Lai Da and others alive to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was ordered to escort Lin Shuangwen and his follower Lai Da, together with other captives, alive to the capital.

sentences.zh: 賴大道病，舒亮令誅之，不稱上意，命仍為護軍統領。

translations.literal: Lai Da fell gravely ill on the road; Shu Liang ordered him executed, which did not please the emperor, and he was ordered to remain colonel of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Da fell gravely ill on the road. Shu Liang ordered him put to death, a decision that failed to satisfy the emperor's intent; Shu Liang was therefore left in his former post as colonel of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 敘功，予雲騎尉世職，再圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: For recorded merit he received a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captaincy and again had his portrait placed in the Hall of Purple Glories.
translations.idiomatic: When his merits were reviewed he was granted a hereditary Cloud Cavalry captaincy, and his portrait was once again hung in the Hall of Purple Glories.

sentences.zh: 出為荊州、黑龍江將軍。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as general at Jingzhou and Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posted as general at Jingzhou and then at Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 在黑龍江，坐私市貂皮，奪官，削世職。

translations.literal: In Heilongjiang he was punished for privately trading sable furs, stripped of office, and lost his hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Heilongjiang he was convicted of trading sable furs on his own account, stripped of office, and deprived of his hereditary title.

sentences.zh: 川、陝、楚教匪起，命以三等侍衛從軍。

translations.literal: When sectarian rebels rose in Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Hubei he was ordered to join the army as a third-rank guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the White Lotus rebellion broke out in Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Hubei, he was ordered to take the field again as a third-rank guardsman.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，戰襄陽，再戰劉家集，屢俘斬賊渠。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing year one he fought at Xiangyang, again at Liujiaji, and repeatedly captured and beheaded rebel chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaqing he fought at Xiangyang and again at Liujiaji, repeatedly capturing rebel leaders and executing them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 攻當陽，先登，額中槍，奮進，殺賊千餘，獲其酋，遂克當陽，賜孔雀翎，授鑲藍旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: At the assault on Dangyang he was first over the wall, was shot in the forehead, pressed forward fiercely, killed over a thousand rebels, took their chief, and took Dangyang; he was granted the peacock feather and made Vice Banner Commander of the Bordered Blue Chinese Banner.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Dangyang he was the first man over the wall. A musket ball struck him in the forehead, yet he pressed on, killed more than a thousand rebels, seized their chieftain, and took the city. He was rewarded with the peacock feather and appointed vice banner commander of the Bordered Blue Chinese Banner.

sentences.zh: 賊自鍾祥分竄唐、鄧，設伏呂堰驛，西竄賊殲焉；

translations.literal: Rebels split from Zhongxiang fleeing toward Tang and Deng, set an ambush at Lüyan Post, and the western contingent was annihilated;
translations.idiomatic: Rebel forces that had split off from Zhongxiang fled toward Tang and Deng, laying an ambush at Lüyan Post; the western column was wiped out there.

sentences.zh: 乃合兵逐東竄賊，戰草店，復中槍，賚銀絲盒、荷包。

translations.literal: then he combined forces to pursue the eastern fugitives, fought at Cao Store, was shot again, and was rewarded with a silver-thread box and a purse.
translations.idiomatic: He then united his troops to pursue the eastern fugitives, fought them at Cao Store, was wounded by gunfire again, and was rewarded with a silver-thread box and an embroidered purse.

sentences.zh: 旋以縱賊渡滾河，奪孔雀翎、巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Soon after, for letting rebels cross the Gun River, his peacock feather and Batulu title were revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, because he had allowed rebel bands to cross the Gun River, his peacock feather and Batulu title were taken from him.

sentences.zh: 二年，坐賊渡漢江，降三品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the second year, because rebels crossed the Han River, he was demoted to third-rank coral knob.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, after rebels crossed the Han River on his watch, he was reduced to the insignia of a third-rank official.

sentences.zh: 三年，復以總督勒保劾勦賊不力，奪官，以兵丁留軍。

translations.literal: In the third year Governor-General Lebao again impeached him for ineffective pursuit of rebels; he was dismissed but kept his soldiers with the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Governor-General Lebao impeached him again for slack pursuit of the rebels. He was stripped of office but allowed to remain with the army as a common soldier.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: He soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 論曰：林爽文亂起，常青及福州將軍恆瑞並水陸二提督，躬率師東渡，徘徊坐誤。

translations.literal: The judgment says: When Lin Shuangwen's rebellion broke out, Chang Qing together with Fuzhou General Hengrui and both naval and land commanders-in-chief personally led troops east across the sea, yet lingered in hesitation and sat by while opportunity was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The historians remark: When Lin Shuangwen's rebellion erupted, Chang Qing, together with Fuzhou general Hengrui and both the naval and land commanders-in-chief, personally led troops across the strait to Taiwan, yet hung back in indecision and let the critical moment slip away.

sentences.zh: 高宗爵柴大紀，誅郝壯猷，欲以激勵諸將；

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong ennobled Chai Daji and executed Hao Zhuangyou, intending thereby to spur the generals;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong ennobled Chai Daji and executed Hao Zhuangyou, intending by reward and punishment alike to stir the other commanders to action.

sentences.zh: 繼以元枚代，功未竟而卒，終煩禁旅，始克底定。

translations.literal: Yuanmei succeeded him, but died before the task was finished, and only after troubling the imperial guards was the affair finally brought to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmei was sent to replace him, but died before the work was done; in the end it required the dispatch of the capital garrisons before the rebellion could be brought to rest.

sentences.zh: 承平久，水陸諸軍不足用，不得獨為大紀罪也。

translations.literal: After long peace the naval and army forces were inadequate, and Chai Daji alone cannot bear all the blame.
translations.idiomatic: After decades of peace the provincial land and naval forces had grown unfit for hard campaigning, and the fault cannot be laid on Chai Daji alone.

sentences.zh: 鄂輝、舒亮從福康安出師，與攀龍、朝雄皆有戰績；

translations.literal: E Hui and Shu Liang followed Fuk'anggan on campaign, and Panlong and Chaogui each had battle achievements;
translations.idiomatic: E Hui and Shu Liang marched under Fuk'anggan, and Panlong and Chaogui each won his share of battlefield credit.

sentences.zh: 然大紀力保危城，當時聲譽遠出諸將上。

translations.literal: yet Daji's desperate defense of the endangered city won him a reputation far above the other generals of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chai Daji's tenacious defense of the besieged city won him a reputation that far outshone every other commander of the day.

sentences.zh: 功名之際，有幸有不幸，固如是夫！

translations.literal: In the matter of fame and fortune there is luck and there is misfortune—it has always been thus!
translations.idiomatic: In the pursuit of fame and reward, some men are fortunate and others are not—has it not always been so?
